+`Result.failure()` reduces a dispatch to one line of prose, but "a rate limit"
+and "a broken gate" can read almost the same in prose while calling for
+opposite responses: retry the first, escalate on the second. `errors.py`
+classifies every not-ok result into exactly one `kind`, checked in this fixed
+order (first match wins, so a cap kill that also timed out is `cap`, and a
+fleet error that mentions a rate limit is `rate_limit`, not `fleet_error`):
+`interrupted` and `cancelled` are conductor's own stop signals; `cap` covers
+a budget exceeded, a cap unenforced (the run came back unpriced against a
+cap), and a watcher's cap kill; `breaker` is any of the four progress
+breakers tripping; `setup` is a `setup` command that failed or timed out;
+`refused` is conductor declining to spawn at all (an isolation failure, a
+ports or include refusal, a non-repo write target, and the rest of
+`_refused_result`'s callers) -- `spawned: false` with an error set.
+`rate_limit`, `transport`, and `refusal` are read from the fleet's own error
+text (and, for `refusal`, Claude's `subtype`) against a per-fleet substring

+| `rate_limit` | any | `rate limit`, `rate_limit`, `429`, `overloaded`, `529`, `quota`, `resource exhausted`, `too many requests` | Claude budget/rate stops, Codex/Antigravity/Cursor 429s, Anthropic 529 "overloaded", Google "resource exhausted" |

+| `transport` | any | `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EPIPE`, `socket hang up`, `fetch failed`, `network`, `502`, `503`, `504` | node/http transport failures reported by any fleet's own error text |
+| `transport` | `claude` | `stream ended without a result event` | a Claude stream cut short with no final result event |
+| `refusal` | any | `I can't help`, `I cannot help` | the model declining the task outright, verbatim |

+| `refusal` | `claude` | any `subtype` starting `error_` (other than `error_max_budget_usd` and `error_max_turns`) whose text also says `refus`, `cannot help`, or `not able to` | Claude's own refusal subtypes |
+`fleet_error` is any other fleet-reported failure; `exit` a nonzero exit with
+none; `gate` a gate (or its clean replacement) that ran and did not pass;
+`no_op` a write that moved no bytes; `read_moved_bytes` a read dispatch that
+moved bytes anyway; `no_answer` a read dispatch with no answer; `commit` a
+requested commit that did not land; `unknown` is anything else. `error_kind`
